placeholders.page_url: The full URL of this page
placeholders.page_title: The page's title (the H1 or the SEO title)
placeholders.site_url: The site's home page URL, ending in a slash
placeholders.business_id: The business node's @id, the same value the Home template uses
placeholders.procedure_name: The name of the treatment this page is about
placeholders.procedure_description: The treatment's description, copied from the page's introduction
placeholders.breadcrumb_1_name: Name of the first breadcrumb level (the parent page)
placeholders.breadcrumb_1_url: URL of the first breadcrumb level
placeholders.breadcrumb_2_name: Name of the second breadcrumb level (this page)
placeholders.breadcrumb_2_url: URL of the second breadcrumb level (this page)
placeholders.faq_1_question: The first FAQ question on the page
placeholders.faq_1_answer: Its answer, exactly as shown on the page
placeholders.faq_2_question: The second FAQ question on the page
placeholders.faq_2_answer: Its answer, exactly as shown on the page
placeholders.rating_value: The average rating shown on the page
placeholders.review_count: The number of reviews behind that rating
placeholders.review_1_author: Name of the first review's author
placeholders.review_1_rating: Star rating of the first review

notes: Include a block only if the page has it: FAQPage needs an FAQ section on the page; the review block needs reviews shown on the page. A page without them uses the template without those blocks.
Repeat: the ListItem for each breadcrumb level (a Sub-Service or Brand / Device page has one more level than a Service page), each Question for each FAQ, and each Review for each review shown.
The business node here only adds reviews. Its other details (name, address, phone, hours, sameAs) live on the Home page and are joined to it by the same @id.
Reviews and ratings of a business that are shown on its own website are valid schema.org markup, but Google does not show review stars for them.
